headline: Oil & gas carries the KSE-100 to a fresh green close on PPL's Sindh discovery, while banks and cement cool off even with the rate backdrop still in their favour.
summary: The KSE-100 closed green again today, up 0.22% to roughly 180,502, with oil & gas stocks doing the heavy lifting after PPL disclosed a new gas find in Sindh — though the flow rates so far are modest. Banks and cement actually pulled back despite a friendly backdrop: T-bill and bond yields still sit comfortably above the policy rate, and a top court just handed large taxpayers, banks included, an easier path to offset tax credits. Gold's stubborn safe-haven bid and this week's T-bill auction are the two things keeping the desk from leaning fully risk-on. Net: a constructive rates story, a cautious global mood.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: T-bill (11.70%) and 10-year PIB (12.30%) yields sit comfortably above the SBP's held 11.5% policy rate, and a fresh Constitutional Court ruling just made it easier for large taxpayers — banks included — to offset tax credits against super tax; today's pullback in the sector reads like profit-taking, not a trend change.

sectors.name: Oil & Gas / E&P
sectors.why: Oil & gas was today's best-performing sector after PPL's Sindh gas discovery, Brent is still up on the month, and the desk's geo-risk radar separately flags E&P (OGDC/PPL/MARI) as the direct beneficiary of the current crude trend.

sectors.name: OMCs & Refineries
sectors.why: Brent's persistent climb plus gold's safe-haven bid both argue for caution here, and names like ATRL and CNERGY already look stretched after big recent runs — CNERGY's 14-day RSI is near 86, deep overbought territory.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: July dispatch data was genuinely strong (domestic volumes +17% YoY) and FCCL just posted a record FY26 profit, but cement was one of today's weaker sectors and valuations across FCCL, LUCK and MLCF screen as 'mixed', not cheap.

sectors.name: Textiles / exporters
sectors.why: FY26 closed with a current-account deficit despite record remittances, and there's no fresher trade data yet to call whether FY27 is turning the corner.

watchlist.angle: The desk's OBV-divergence-up strategy just fired on BML with a high-confidence read — volume building ahead of price, right 96.6% of the time across 89 historical signals (net expectancy +5.11%). Fundamentals back it up: BML screens 'attractive', cheap at 6.5x earnings with a strong 32% net margin. A results date is estimated around Aug 28, though that date is an unconfirmed scrape, not a filed notice.
watchlist.risk: No dividend, so the whole case rests on the stock re-rating rather than a payout cushion — if the results date slips or disappoints, there's no income floor underneath it.

watchlist.angle: PPL disclosed a gas & condensate find at its Dolphin X-1 well in Sindh today, and oil & gas was the exchange's best-performing sector as a result; the desk's geo-risk radar separately names PPL (with OGDC and MARI) as a beneficiary of the current Brent trend. Fundamentals screen 'mixed' but with a strong 34% net margin and an improving forward P/E (6.1x vs 8.0x trailing).
watchlist.risk: The disclosed flow rates are modest — 0.942 mmscfd of gas, and condensate that fell from 94 to 46 bbl/day within 24 hours — so the 'major win' headline is ahead of the actual reservoir data, and there's no confirmed technical trigger behind the move, just a news reaction.

watchlist.angle: A quiet-base ATR breakout trigger just fired on GAL, and the fundamentals are a reasonable match — cheap at 5.5x earnings with a healthy 13% net margin, rated 'mixed' overall. As an auto assembler, it also rides any pickup in car sales.
watchlist.risk: The signal is low-confidence with only 10 historical instances backing it, GAL is small-cap and thin-volume, and the next dated catalyst (results, estimated late September) is both unconfirmed and a long way off.

watchlist.angle: Fauji Cement just posted its highest-ever FY26 profit and has a confirmed book-closure on Aug 22 carrying a Rs1.5 dividend. This is a fundamentals-and-catalyst story rather than a technical one — no live strategy trigger is currently firing on the name.
watchlist.risk: Cement was one of today's weaker sectors even with FCCL's good news, and the fundamental read is only 'mixed' (fair valuation, not cheap) — sentiment could stay cool despite the headline numbers.

catalysts.event: SBP weekly FX reserves print — watched for whether the recovery streak extends
MSCI Frontier Market Small Cap reconstitution effective (AIRLINK added, Biafo removed)

risks: Gold's persistent safe-haven bid (+10.75% over the past month) and a small VIX uptick both suggest foreign flows could stay cautious rather than chase PSX higher.

PIB yields rose across every tenor at the last auction even as CPI decelerated — the bond market is pricing a more hawkish path than the headline inflation number suggests, which could cap the banks/carry-trade thesis.
The Aug 19 T-bill auction and the Aug 21 reserves print are the next real tests of the 'macro is stabilising' story — a weak result on either could flip today's mild optimism.
